title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a typed sheet, page '- 21 -', printed upside down. It was evidently reused as scrap paper for the handwritten notes on abelian varieties and Néron–Severi groups on the neighbouring pages. It is a fragment of a systematic exposition of cohomology on sites (a category C with a topology) and has nothing to do with algebraic cycles.

Setting.
- A is a ring.
- H^0 : C~_A → C^_A is the inclusion of sheaves of A-modules into presheaves of A-modules.
- \bar H^0 : C~_Ab → C^_Ab is the corresponding inclusion for abelian sheaves.
- The right derived functors are the presheaf-valued cohomology functors ℋ^q(F) : X ↦ H^q(X,F).

What is proved.
- Claim: for a sheaf of A-modules F, the derived functors of H^0 computed in A-modules agree with those of \bar H^0 computed on the underlying abelian sheaf.
- Reduction: it suffices to show that the forgetful functor sends H^0-acyclic A-Modules to \bar H^0-acyclic abelian sheaves. This works because the forgetful functor is exact and commutes with the inclusion, so one can compute with injective resolutions of A-Modules.
- Step 1: Corollary (2.5) is a Čech-type criterion. It says ℋ^q(F)=0 for q>0 iff the Čech cohomology Ȟ^q(X, H^0(F)) vanishes for q>0 and all X, Ȟ being the derived Čech functors on presheaves. So F being H^0-acyclic gives Ȟ^q(X,H^0(F))=0 in presheaves of A-modules.
- Step 2: Proposition (1.5) and formula (15) say Čech cohomology is computed by an explicit filtered colimit of Čech complexes over covering sieves. That computation commutes with forgetting the A-module structure, so the same vanishing holds in presheaves of abelian groups.
- Step 3: applying Corollary (2.5) again in the abelian setting gives ℋ^q(F)=0 for q>0.

The page then opens '§3. Critères d'acyclicité', announcing a first family of acyclic sheaves. This is exactly the architecture of SGA 4 Exposé V (Verdier, Cohomologie dans les topos), where Čech-based acyclicity criteria precede flasque sheaves. The sheet is likely a typescript draft of SGA 4 V or of closely related seminar notes (Grothendieck–Verdier), not of the cycles notes.
errors: No mathematical error. The final line should strictly read ℋ^q(F̲)=0, the underlying abelian sheaf, in the abelian category; the typescript, or its transcription, drops the underline.
The argument tacitly uses that Corollary (2.5) holds in both the A-module and the abelian setting, and that the forgetful functor commutes with sheafification and the Čech colimit. Both are standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reused typed sheet from an exposition of standard site cohomology (essentially SGA 4 V material), unrelated to the cycles notes written on its reverse. It contains only routine, published homological algebra.
transcription_corrections: The page is printed upside down. It is the verso of scrap paper, a typescript page numbered '- 21 -', not part of the handwritten cycles notes.
The target of the first displayed functor is the presheaf category C^_Ab (hat), and the source is the sheaf category C~_Ab (tilde).

'Il suffit évidemment de montrer que si F est un A-Module acyclique pour H^0, alors F̲ est acyclique pour \bar H^0' – the underline marks the underlying abelian sheaf, and the second functor is \bar H^0.
The final conclusion should be ℋ^q(F̲)=0 (0<q), i.e. the abelian version, presumably \bar ℋ^q.
The heading is 'N° 3. Critères d'acyclicité' and is underlined. The last line is 'acycliques.' followed by '.../...'.
